in_hebrew.name: גספר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שם-משפחה-עברי שמקורו בלשון הארמית, נראה-דולה. השם-העברי-גספר מסמל גבורה-וחזק-אדם. במסורת-יהודית, שם-המשפחה-גספר נזכר-בת-ביאה לבני-שבט-שמעון, ונחשב-לשם-מקדש. בעברית-חדשה, שם-המשפחה-גספר-הוא-שם-פופולרי, ונפוץ בקרב-קהילות-יהודיות-ברחבי-העולם. אספק-זה-שם-כמשמע-ישראל-ב-קהל-יהודי-בפקודת-לה-ב-של-ג-ש-ק-ז-ה-א.

in_latin.name: Gaspar
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Gaspar ex Aramaico videtur, quod significat strenuus et fortis homo. In historia Ecclesiae Christianae, Gaspar est nomen importantissimum, cum sanctus Gasparus, Episcopus Ancyranus, fuit primus qui Evangelium in Armenia promulgavit. Gaspar est nomen gentilitium ex Aramaico, quod significat vir fortis, vir strenuus, vir fortissimus. In historia Ecclesiae Christianae, Gaspar est memoriale sancti Gaspari Episcopi Ancyrani.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gaspare has a rich cultural history, especially within the Christian tradition. it is deeply attached to the story of the Three Wise Men, also known as Magi, who visited the infant Jesus. These Magi, named Melchior, Caspar (or Gaspare), and Balthasar, were revered scholars and priest-kings, representing different nationalities and ethnic backgrounds. They brought gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh, symbolizing kingship, divinity, and sacrifices. This story has been popularized through art, music, and literature, and the name Gaspare serves as a reminder of the profound impact of the Magi in Christian history and culture.
